Preserved Primary Document • concl-w1.htm
William Concilor was the grandson of Thomas Concilor who died in
. His parents are not yet known. It is possible he was the son of Thomas's daughter, Mary Consela, or he might have been the son of a deceased child of Thomas's.
On February 12,

William bought land from John Durham and his wife Elizabeth for 75 pounds. This land adjoined John Durham's lands in Little Creek Hundred in Kent Co. and marked the documented beginning of a long term friendship between the Durhams and the Concilors although the families probably knew each other prior to this. At any rate, 2 of John Durham's daughters would eventually marry Concilors (possible sons of William and his wife, Mary).
The connection with the Durham family continued when, on December 16,
, William signed papers along with  Daniel Durham  whereby John Durham and Sarah Handsor (John's sister?) were name administrators of the estate of Sarah's deceased husband  William Hansor .
On November 28,
Willam and his wife, Mary, of Little Creek Hundred sold 100 acres of land to Francis Barber for 200 pounds. This is probably the same 100 acres William purchased from John Durham in
In
, William Concilor died and on May 1,
Administration of  his estate  was given to his long time friend and neighbor, John Durham. The papers mention expenses for clothing  Whittenton and William Conselor .
We have no confirmed children of William and Mary but there were other Concilors in the area at the time who were possible descendants of William.
Possible children of William and Mary Concilor:
Elijah Concilor appeared in the Duck Creek Hundred 			taxables for
and
. He married Hannah Durham, daughter of  John Durham .
John Concilor appeared in the Murderkill Hundred taxables for
and
. 	  Thomas Concilor appeared in the
Murderkill Hundred taxables, the
Dover Hundred taxables and the
census.
Charles Concilor appeared in the
Little Creek Hundred taxables. It is 		believed he moved to New Jersey around
when he married Margaret Teel in 			Salem on
14 September 1809
There was also a second Thomas Concilor in the area since two are listed in the
Taxables (one in Murderkill Hundred and one in Little Creek Hundred so we cannot know for sure whch one married John Durham's daughter, Elizabeth.
Yet another Thomas Concilor  was born in Kent Co. on
7 March 1784

. He and his wife Mary were tenants on a farm in Duck Creek Hundred called Bloomsbury before moving to Salem Co., NJ.   Bloomsbury has been excavated by archeologist Ned Heite and a report will be printed shortly. For more information on  Bloomsbury, visit Ned's website. For more information about the Bloomsbury Thomas Concilor and other Concilors, visit Betty and Ray Terrys site  Mitsawokett.

Concilor

Preserved Primary Document • concl-w1.htm

William Concilor was the grandson of Thomas Concilor who died in 1739. His parents are not yet known. It is possible he was the son of Thomas's daughter, Mary Consela, or he might have been the son of a deceased child of Thomas's. On February 12, 1756 William bought land from John Durham and his wife Elizabeth for 75 pounds. This land adjoined John Durham's lands in Little Creek Hundred in Kent Co. and marked the documented beginning of a long term friendship between the Durhams and the Concilors although the families probably knew each other prior to this. At any rate, 2 of John Durham's daughters would eventually marry Concilors (possible sons of William and his wife, Mary). The connection with the Durham family continued when, on December 16, 1767, William signed papers along with Daniel Durham whereby John Durham and Sarah Handsor (John's sister?) were name administrators of the estate of Sarah's deceased husband William Hansor . On November 28, 1776 Willam and his wife, Mary, of Little Creek Hundred sold 100 acres of land to Francis Barber for 200 pounds. This is probably the same 100 acres William purchased from John Durham in 1756. In 1780, William Concilor died and on May 1, 1780 Administration of his estate was given to his long time friend and neighbor, John Durham. The papers mention expenses for clothing Whittenton and William Conselor . We have no confirmed children of William and Mary but there were other Concilors in the area at the time who were possible descendants of William. Possible children of William and Mary Concilor: Elijah Concilor appeared in the Duck Creek Hundred taxables for 1783 and 1788. He married Hannah Durham, daughter of John Durham . John Concilor appeared in the Murderkill Hundred taxables for 1782 and 1790. Thomas Concilor appeared in the 1782 Murderkill Hundred taxables, the 1790 Dover Hundred taxables and the 1800 census. Charles Concilor appeared in the 1782 Little Creek Hundred taxables. It is believed he moved to New Jersey around 1809 when he married Margaret Teel in Salem on 14 September 1809. There was also a second Thomas Concilor in the area since two are listed in the 1782 Taxables (one in Murderkill Hundred and one in Little Creek Hundred so we cannot know for sure whch one married John Durham's daughter, Elizabeth. Yet another Thomas Concilor was born in Kent Co. on 7 March 1784. He and his wife Mary were tenants on a farm in Duck Creek Hundred called Bloomsbury before moving to Salem Co., NJ. Bloomsbury has been excavated by archeologist Ned Heite and a report will be printed shortly. For more information on Bloomsbury, visit Ned's website. For more information about the Bloomsbury Thomas Concilor and other Concilors, visit Betty and Ray Terrys site Mitsawokett. The 1800 DE Federal Census lists Elijah Councilor, Charles Councilor, Jeremiah Councilor and Thomas Councilor, all living in Kent Co.
